posts.title: Does Ruby on Rails still make sense?
posts.description: Someone asked me, given that LLMs exist and likely keep improving, whether I thought Ruby on Rails still made sense? The implication being of course that writing code is now extremely cheap and you can build anything you like in any language, so why not choose to rewrite everything in Rust? posts.title: On using UUIDs
posts.description: I want to talk about using UUIDs (as primary keys) and why it may be a pretty decent default. Let's first quickly go over all the situations for which we would absolutely need UUIDs: You need primary keys to be generated in a decentralised manner and consolidate them later You need 128 bits and you need a standard format supported in a lot of places You need to support a system already using UUIDs

posts.title: Using an "ORM" for HTML
posts.description: I want to splurge some words about Rails templates. A freshly generated Rails project comes with ERB-based templates for its views. This is totally fine. I've been using them for years now, and I can build nice things with it, I dare say.
